cmd_tiles.text: The six grow about as fast as the industry, but their middle margin and ROCE sit slightly below the Nifty Pharma average, which includes large, more global players such as Sun Pharma and Divi's. The cash cycle is the clearest gap: two companies (Alembic, Ipca) hold far more inventory than the industry.

cmd_map.text: Companies in the top-right (Ajanta, Mankind) combine branded India or chronic portfolios with pricing power. Alembic and Alkem sit bottom-left: Alembic because R&D and new plants weigh on margin, Alkem because of its acute and trade-generics mix. Glenmark's position is flattered by one-off licensing income.

rt_table.text: Green and red mark best and weakest of the six. The Industry column is the Nifty Pharma average, so a company can be best of six and still below the industry.

rt_trend_roce.text: Ajanta has risen steadily on margin. Mankind fell sharply after the BSV acquisition added goodwill to capital. Glenmark's FY26 spike is licensing income. Alembic is flat because new plants are not yet full.

rt_trend_roe.text: ROE follows ROCE. Companies with little debt (Ajanta, Ipca) have ROE close to ROCE; borrowing would lift ROE without improving the business.

rt_trend_roic.text: ROIC is after-tax return on the money invested in operations. Above about 12% (a typical cost of capital for Indian pharma) the company creates value; below it, growth destroys value.

rt_trend_ebitda_margin.text: Margins rose across the industry from FY23 as API and freight costs eased after the pandemic. Companies with branded India portfolios (Ajanta, Mankind) sit highest.

rt_trend_inventory_days.text: API-integrated companies (Alembic, Ipca) hold more stock because they carry raw materials and intermediates as well as finished goods.

rt_trend_debtor_days.text: Debtor days rise when US sales or distributor credit grow. Ajanta's jump (93 to 124) is the sharpest move in FY26.

rt_trend_ccc.text: Cash cycle = inventory + debtor days − payable days. Glenmark's low figure comes from stretching suppliers, which is not sustainable.

rt_trend_de_ratio.text: Debt is low across the set. Mankind rose after the BSV deal; Alembic after funding new plants.

rt_trend_cfo_pat.text: Below 1x means profit is not arriving as cash. Ajanta's 0.5x in FY26 is the warning sign; Glenmark's high figure is licensing cash.

rt_trend_asset_turnover.text: Sales per rupee of assets. Mankind dropped after the BSV deal added assets; Ajanta and Glenmark are highest.

rt_trend_interest_cover.text: Times operating profit covers interest. Very high values mean almost no debt; Mankind's ~4x is the lowest but still safe.

rt_trend_fcf_margin.text: Free cash flow here is cash from operations minus all investing (capex, acquisitions, investments), as a share of sales. Big deal years show as negative.

rt_dupont.text: ROE = profit margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier. Ajanta wins on margin; Mankind's weak spot is asset turnover after BSV; Glenmark uses more liabilities.

rg_fda.text: FDA status decides whether US launches continue. Alkem's Daman OAI is the only open issue; Glenmark and Ajanta have just cleared theirs.

rg_anda.text: More approvals do not mean more revenue: Ajanta earns about 2.3x more US revenue per product than Alembic by choosing products with few competitors.

rg_rnd.text: Higher R&D spend currently goes with lower margins because the payoff from new filings arrives years later.

nw_timeline.text: Regulatory and policy news (FDA, tariffs) moved these companies more than quarterly results did in the last six months.

nw_heat.text: US revenue and EBITDA margin are the two numbers most affected by news; Alkem is the only company with net negative news.

st_map.text: Each number counts how many of a company's five problem statements need that type of consulting help; Digital shows how far behind the company is.

pl_scatter.text: Each dot is one company in one year. With 30 points this is more reliable than one company's 5 years, but it mixes very different business models.

market.text: The Indian pharma market grew ~10% in FY26 (volume 2.7%, price 4.4%, new products 2.8%), with chronic (~14%) well ahead of acute (~8%).
